answer: The latest health-related news on BBC News is 'I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work', published 2026-10-30 (BBC Health section, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm78pxxe55v0o). Main findings: 23-year-old special educational needs teacher Saskia Reeves-Priestley collapsed at work with dizziness, nausea, heart palpitations and feeling hot; blood tests showed her vitamin D level was 'next to nothing'. Vitamin D deficiency is increasingly widespread in the UK, especially among young people - nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient last year according to the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, with girls and young women particularly affected. Most vitamin D is made by the body when UV sunlight hits the skin (diet sources like oily fish, meat and supplements contribute less); reduced sunlight, covering skin, sunscreen and darker skin tones all lower production. Deficiency is linked to rickets in babies and osteomalacia (bone weakening) in adults. Recommendations: get safe sunlight exposure, consider dietary sources/supplements of vitamin D (doctors will offer supplements to high-risk patients who are concerned), and be aware symptoms can be difficult to spot and easily missed.
